newsitem.title: TURKEY: Turkish shares gain 1.14 pct on selective buys.
newsitem.headline: Turkish shares gain 1.14 pct on selective buys.

text.p: Istanbul shares rose an average 1.14 percent in selective buying on Wednesday in a technical rebound after recent drops, brokers said.
The IMKB-100 .ISEC closed 1,068.10 points higher at 94,735.34 and compared to last Friday's close of 94,879.14. It had lost 1.28 percent in the last two days after last week's 6.2 percent surge.
Trade volume firmed to 11.70 trillion lira from Tuesday's nine trillion lira.

"The market was extremely quiet on Monday and Tuesday. But sales were not as strong as expected, so the market recovered with the help of Prime Minister's comments on the Telekom sell-off," said Taner Mirza from Esbank.
Prime Minister Necmettin Erbakan said Turk Telekom's privatisation was progressing according to a law debated by the constitutional court since late November.

The court meets once a week and it is not known when it will rule. Erbakan told reporters that a new legal framework would be quickly constructed if the court decided to cancel the law currently in effect.

The market was also cautious earlier in the week due to the possibility of an extended new year holiday. Earlier press reports had said the government might extend the holiday to five days from December 27 to January 2 by declaring December 30 and 31 official holiday. But no such announcement was made.

Of the 232 shares traded, gainers outdid losers sharply by 115 to 42 and 75 ended stable. The 85-share industrial index .ISEI rose 1.14 percent to 101,890.96 and the 15-share financial index .ISEF put on 1.13 percent to 88,047.61.

Actives were again led by largely state-owned firms and utilities -- Aktas Elektrik, up 3,000 lira to 92,000, petroleum refiner Tupras, up 250 lira to 26,000, Cukurova Elektrik, up 2,500 lira to 132,500 and flat steel giant Eregli, up 250 lira at 12,750.
Together, the four stocks made up 24.8 percent of the total turnover.
